value.title: Two-letter support pruning
value.summary: Establish rigorously scoped restrictions on the super-input support of candidate two-letter Marton improvements.
conditions: The accepted pruning result is conditional on the explicitly assumed Geng--Jog--Nair--Wang binary-input Marton sum-rate theorem.

value.title: Two-letter Marton two-symbol support pruning
value.summary:
Accepted statement:

Assume the Geng--Jog--Nair--Wang theorem that Marton's private-message sum-rate for every binary-input broadcast channel equals randomized time division. For the half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}, every finite Marton law whose induced super-input X_1X_2 is supported on at most two of {00,01,10,11} has sum-rate strictly below 0.615 bits. Consequently, because the product randomized-time-division value is greater than 0.7232857688439092 bits, every strict two-letter Marton improvement over the current BSSC achievable rate must use at least three super-input symbols. This is only a support-pruning result and does not rule out a gain on three- or four-symbol support.

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- Validity is conditional on the Geng–Jog–Nair–Wang theorem explicitly assumed in the claim.
- The numerical product RTD benchmark is treated as supplied problem data; the execution attestation does not independently prove it.
- The result only excludes supports of cardinality at most two and makes no assertion against gains using three- or four-symbol support.

value.title: Support-orbit, cooperation, and repetition-subchannel proof
value.summary: Proof used to establish the linked accepted claim. It exhausts singleton and two-symbol super-input supports through the adjacent, antirepetition, and repetition symmetry classes; applies cooperative binary-erasure bounds to the first two classes; and, conditional on the explicitly assumed binary-input Marton theorem, reduces the repetition class to randomized time division. Concavity, reflection symmetry, and a global tangent bound then give the strict 0.615-bit threshold. This proof item is limited to the linked support-pruning claim and does not address three- or four-symbol support.

value.title: Exact support-orbit and directed-interval audit tool
value.summary: Tool used for the computationally audited portion of the linked accepted claim. It uses exact rational arithmetic to construct the product receiver marginals, classify all six two-symbol supports, and verify the transition structures used by the proof. It also uses directed high-precision decimal intervals to check the repetition-orbit tangent certificate and the strict separation below 0.615. The tool does not independently prove the supplied product randomized-time-division benchmark or the assumed Geng--Jog--Nair--Wang theorem.

placementAudits.rationale: The accepted claim is a structural restriction on candidate two-letter Marton achievable-rate improvements, so its narrowest coherent placement is the non-root multiletter Marton achievability program rather than any existing converse program.
